analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials peak EPS 29 Oct 2026
key_insights: S&P futures down 20bps pre-market on technology earnings. GOOGL down 10% pre-market. Samsung disappointed on lack of a new shareholder return plan, KOSPI closed down 124bps. Europe up 50-75bps. ECB today, BOJ Friday, FOMC was yesterday, PCE is released today.

Crude down 2% with WTI approaching $100 and Brent $113 on fresh diplomatic efforts in the Middle East to avoid a potential restart of US military strikes on Iran. European gas down 4% to $97 after hitting $100 yesterday. The 10-year is just below 5%, the dollar is flat, and Bitcoin is down 150bps to $80k.

CAT is the standout, down 10% pre-market. Q3 EPS $7.20 vs $7.10 consensus, EBIT $4.26bn vs $4.09bn, sales $20.68bn in line, backlog $78bn in line. The desk thinks the tide has turned: 2027 should bring higher earnings but weaker backlog and orders against tough comps, and the debate is where the multiple settles.

AGCO: the desk says fade ag as crop prices roll over. Q3 EPS $1.05 vs $0.87 beat, but full-year sales guide cut to $9.8-10bn from $10.1-10.2bn, full-year EPS $5.50 vs $5.50-5.75 prior, and the implied Q4 exit rate is weaker. DE reports in late November.

PWR is the go-to long-only name in the space. Q3 EPS $6.06 vs $4.99, EBITDA $1.45bn vs $1.22bn, backlog $64bn up 63% y/y, full-year EPS raised to $17.90-18.30 from $16.45-16.95. The desk says grid demand is not only AI, and the debate is the multiple and finding other grid names that are more than AI.

TT is expected to be dinged on the Q4 guide. Q3 EPS $4.86 vs $4.73, revenue $6.76bn vs $6.5bn, bookings $7.25bn, full-year EPS reaffirmed at $15.20-15.30. The multiple is elevated, investors are pushing non-resi HVAC higher and resi lower, and the desk thinks investors are either long both JCI and TT or long JCI with TT as a hedge.

WCC: Q3 EPS $5.77 vs $4.70, revenue $7.23bn vs $6.87bn, EBITDA $562mm vs $491mm, organic growth 17%, full-year organic growth guide raised to 13-14% from 9-11% and EPS to $18-18.5 from $16-17.50. At 18x EPS and 11x EBITDA, both at or above the high end of the recent range, the debate is what to pay.
Residential HVAC remains a source of funds, with CARR the most debated. CARR Q3 EPS $0.87 vs $0.76 included $130mm of EBIT from IEEPA refunds, and the Q4 guide implies a lower quarter.
Defense is catching a bid. HII Q3 EPS $5.48 vs $4.36, with $32.4bn of contract awards. LHX Q3 EPS $3.28 vs $2.95, orders of $19bn, record backlog of $53.2bn and book-to-bill of 3.2x.

Weak prints in building products and materials: CRH cut full-year EBITDA guide to $7.8-8bn from $8.1-8.5bn and is a very crowded long. VMC cut full-year EBITDA to $2.4bn, with aggregates gross profit $593mm vs $617mm. DHI guided fiscal 2027 revenue to $30-32bn vs $34bn consensus with gross margin of 19.5% vs 20.5%.

OSK missed badly: Q3 EPS $2.41 vs $3.06 consensus, full-year EPS cut to $8.50-9.50 from $11, with weakness in Vocational and a much lower implied Q4. AXTA Q3 EBITDA $282mm vs $299mm, with Q4 EBITDA guide $254-264mm vs $286mm consensus.

sector_views.rationale: Remains a source of funds, with investors pushing non-resi HVAC higher and resi lower.
Crop prices are rolling over and the desk sees more reasons to sell than buy on macro and micro.
VMC and CRH guided lower, and aggregates weakness is unexpected on both an absolute and a relative basis.
Defense is catching a bid, with LHX and HII reporting strong orders and backlog.
PWR shows grid demand is not only AI, and it is the go-to long-only name.

earnings_insights: AGCO Q3 reported EPS $1.05 vs $0.87 consensus, sales $2.3bn in line, EBITDA $137mm vs $140mm consensus. Full-year sales guide $9.8-10bn vs $10.1-10.2bn prior. Full-year EPS $5.50 vs $5.50-5.75 prior.
CAT Q3 reported EPS $7.20 vs $7.10 consensus, EBIT $4.26bn vs $4.09bn consensus, sales $20.68bn in line, backlog $78bn. Implied move 6%.

PWR Q3 reported EPS $6.06 vs $4.99 consensus, EBITDA $1.45bn vs $1.22bn, backlog $64bn up 63% y/y. Full-year EPS $17.90-18.30 vs $16.45-16.95 prior, revenue $41.3-41.6bn vs $39.3-39.7bn prior, EBITDA $4.4-4.49bn vs $4.09-4.21bn prior.
WCC Q3 reported EPS $5.77 vs $4.70 consensus, revenue $7.23bn vs $6.87bn, EBITDA $562mm vs $491mm, organic growth 17%. Full-year EPS $18-18.5 vs $16-17.50 prior, organic growth 13-14% vs 9-11% prior.
TT Q3 reported EPS $4.86 vs $4.73 consensus, revenue $6.76bn vs $6.5bn, bookings $7.25bn, EBITDA $1.45bn in line. Full-year EPS $15.20-15.30 reaffirmed, with revenue growth 13.5% vs 11.5% prior.
CARR Q3 EPS $0.87 vs $0.76 consensus including $130mm of EBIT from IEEPA refunds, EBIT $1.09bn vs $975mm. Full-year EPS guide $2.85-2.90 vs $2.90 prior, revenue $23.8-24bn vs $23bn prior.

DHI fiscal Q4 EPS $2.67, revenue $9.37bn vs $9.07bn, gross margin 19.5% vs 20.5% expected. Fiscal 2027 revenue guide $30-32bn vs $34bn consensus on 79-84k closings. Cash flow from operations $3.5bn, repurchases $3bn.
HII Q3 EPS $5.48 vs $4.36 consensus, revenue $3.54bn vs $3.38bn, new awards $32.4bn. FY26 shipbuilding revenue guide $10.5-10.7bn vs $10.2-10.4bn prior.
LHX Q3 EPS $3.28 vs $2.95 consensus, revenue $6.06bn vs $5.92bn, organic growth 9%, orders $19bn, record backlog $53.2bn, book-to-bill 3.2x. Full-year EPS $12.25-12.35 vs $11.80-12 prior.
OSK Q3 EPS $2.41 vs $3.06 consensus, sales $2.84bn vs $2.92bn. Full-year EPS $8.50-9.50 vs $11 prior.
CRH Q3 EBITDA $2.68bn vs $2.72bn consensus, revenue $11.40bn vs $11.56bn. Full-year EBITDA guide $7.8-8bn vs $8.1-8.5bn prior, EPS reaffirmed.
VMC Q3 EPS $2.83 vs $2.81 consensus, revenue under $2.19bn vs $2.24bn, EBITDA $707mm vs $706mm. Full-year EBITDA guide $2.4bn vs $2.4-2.6bn prior.
AXTA Q3 EBITDA $282mm vs $299mm consensus, revenue $1.311bn vs $1.33bn. Q4 EBITDA guide $254-264mm vs $286mm consensus.
ENTG Q3 EPS $1.23 vs $1.03 consensus, sales $1.01bn vs $925mm. Q4 EPS guide $1.32-1.40 vs $1.12 consensus, sales $1.03-1.06bn vs $962mm consensus.
EME Q3 EPS $9.04 vs $8.34 consensus, sales $5.54bn vs $5.19bn. Full-year revenue guide $20.6-21bn.
HWM Q3 EPS $1.46 vs $1.36 consensus, revenue $2.7bn vs $2.6bn, EBITDA $879mm vs $837mm. Full-year EPS guide $5.49-5.51 vs $5.23-5.31 prior.
ATI Q3 EPS $1.46 beat, EBITDA $328mm vs $312mm. Full-year EBITDA raised to $1.19-1.2bn from $1.14-1.19bn prior, EPS $5.17-5.23 vs $4.60-5.18 prior.
BLDR Q3 EPS $1.51 vs $1.06 consensus, revenue $3.85bn vs $3.75bn, EBITDA $311mm vs $299mm. Full-year revenue narrowed to $14.2-14.6bn and EBITDA to $1.07-1.125bn.
AOS Q3 EPS $0.93 vs $0.90 consensus, sales $941mm vs $960mm consensus. Full-year EPS guide $3.42-3.52 (excluding China) vs $3.70-3.85 prior.
LIN Q3 revenue $9.4bn vs $9.16bn consensus, adjusted EPS $4.59 vs $4.52 consensus. Full-year adjusted EPS guide $17.82-17.92 vs $17.70-17.90 prior. Project backlog $11bn.
LKQ Q3 EPS $0.50 vs $0.61 consensus, revenue $3.32bn in line.
KBR Q3 EPS $1.12 vs $1 consensus, EBITDA $268mm vs $247mm, book-to-bill 0.9x. Full-year EBITDA $980mm-1.04bn.
European results: MTX Q3 roughly in line, shares -4%. IMI raised guidance, shares +1%. PRY Q3 beat and raise, shares +1%. AI FP sales at a four-year high, shares +3%. AIR FP in line, shares +3%.
